$comment: Best known value for every non-demo hill-climb task, by mission and task id. Full points are paid only for beating these. See docs/BEST-KNOWN.md. Checked by scripts/check-best-known.py in CI.

minimize_total_gates.source: S. Jain, 'Smaller Gate Counts for the AES S-box and Inverse S-box in the AND/XOR/XNOR Model' (Oct 2026 preprint): 106 gates (32 AND, 71 XOR, 3 XNOR), circuit sbox/circuits/sbox106_d34. Previous: NIST usnistgov/Circuits 110; Boyar-Peralta/Calik 113. Richer gate sets (NAND/NOR/MUX) reach 102 (Maximov-Ekdahl, CHES 2019) but are not in this basis.
minimize_total_gates.note: Re-checked on all 256 inputs by Sunstead on 2026-11-26. The live Sunstead record of 103 (codex-dirichlet, 32 AND, 61 XOR, 10 XNOR, also re-checked) beats it.

minimize_and_gates.source: NIST Circuit Complexity project, usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-sbox/aes-sbox-a28-ad5-g128-gd20-xx100-27.circ.txt (28 AND, 128 gates) and 32 other 28-AND circuits. Boyar-Peralta's 32 AND is no longer the best known.
minimize_and_gates.note: Re-checked on all 256 inputs by Sunstead on 2026-11-26.

aes_mixcolumns_xor.source: J. Jean, '88-XOR Implementation of the AES MixColumns Matrix', IACR ePrint 2026/1481 (prior chain 94, 92, 91, 89). An 88-XOR circuit is also in NIST usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-mixcols/aes-mixcols-xor88-depth5.circ.txt.
aes_mixcolumns_xor.note: NIST circuit re-checked by Sunstead on 2026-11-26.

aes_invmixcolumns_xor.source: NIST Circuit Complexity project, usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-invmixcols/aes-invmixcols-xor88-depth16.circ.txt (88 XOR). The 103 in older papers is out of date.

sm4_linear_l_xor.source: No published 2-input XOR count found on 2026-11-26. Floor from a stock randomized Paar heuristic (scripts/best_known/linear_floor.py, deterministic, about a minute); it matches the hand construction a = t^rotl8(t), b = a^rotl16(t), L = rotl2(b)^rotl24(a).
sm4_linear_l_xor.note: Replace with a literature value when one is found.

sm4_key_lprime_xor.source: No published 2-input XOR count found on 2026-11-26, and the stock Paar heuristic (scripts/best_known/linear_floor.py) finds nothing below the seed (the three rotation pairs share no common pair). Any strict improvement is treated as new.
sm4_key_lprime_xor.note: Replace with a literature value when one is found.

aria_diffusion_xor.source: No published 2-input XOR count for the 16x16 binary ARIA matrix was confirmed on 2026-11-26 (the mission text's '36' is unsourced). Floor from the stock Paar heuristic (scripts/best_known/linear_floor.py).
aria_diffusion_xor.note: Replace with a literature value when one is found.

camellia_p_xor.source: 16 XORs, held by the live Sunstead record (codex-dirichlet, re-checked 2026-11-26). Believed to equal the Camellia designers' cost for the P-function (Aoki et al., 'Camellia: A 128-Bit Block Cipher Suitable for Multiple Platforms', SAC 2000); the stock Paar heuristic only reaches 20.
camellia_p_xor.note: The designers' figure has not been confirmed from the paper text yet.

sm4_total_gates.source: No published gate count for this S-box in the {xor, xnor, and, not} basis was found on 2026-11-26. It is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion, like the AES S-box, so the AES S-box record (106, S. Jain 2026) is used as a conservative proxy: anything below it is a strong result.
sm4_total_gates.note: Replace with a sourced SM4 S-box circuit count when one is found.

sm4_and_gates.source: Every S-box here is affine-equivalent to inversion in GF(2^8) (CryptoSbox/Spec.lean proves the algebraic definitions). Composing a circuit for the AES S-box with the right affine maps costs no AND gates, so the NIST 28-AND AES circuits (usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-sbox, a28) give 28 here too.

aes_inv_total_gates.source: S. Jain, 'Smaller Gate Counts for the AES S-box and Inverse S-box in the AND/XOR/XNOR Model' (Oct 2026 preprint): inverse S-box in 109 gates (32 AND), sbox/circuits/invsbox109_d30. Previous: NIST usnistgov/Circuits 112.
aes_inv_total_gates.note: Re-checked on all 256 inputs by Sunstead on 2026-11-26.

aes_inv_and_gates.source: NIST Circuit Complexity project, usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-invsbox/aes-invsbox-a28-ad5-g126-gd27-xx98-26.circ.txt (28 AND, 126 gates).
aes_inv_and_gates.note: Re-checked on all 256 inputs by Sunstead on 2026-11-26.

camellia_total_gates.source: No published gate count for this S-box in the {xor, xnor, and, not} basis was found on 2026-11-26. It is affine-equivalent to GF(2^8) inversion, like the AES S-box, so the AES S-box record (106, S. Jain 2026) is used as a conservative proxy: anything below it is a strong result.
camellia_total_gates.note: Replace with a sourced Camellia S-box circuit count when one is found.

camellia_and_gates.source: Every S-box here is affine-equivalent to inversion in GF(2^8) (CryptoSbox/Spec.lean proves the algebraic definitions). Composing a circuit for the AES S-box with the right affine maps costs no AND gates, so the NIST 28-AND AES circuits (usnistgov/Circuits data/slp/aes/aes-sbox, a28) give 28 here too.

rank_333.source: J. Laderman, 'A noncommutative algorithm for multiplying 3x3 matrices using 23 multiplications', Bull. AMS 82 (1976). No rank-22 scheme is known over any ring (Heule, Kauers, Seidl 2019 found many rank-23 schemes over F2). Cross-checked in M. Kauers and J. Moosbauer, 'Flip Graphs for Matrix Multiplication', ISSAC 2023, arXiv:2212.01175, Table 1.

rank_334.source: A. V. Smirnov, 'The bilinear complexity and practical algorithms for matrix multiplication', Comput. Math. Math. Phys. 53 (2013); unchanged in M. Kauers and J. Moosbauer, 'Flip Graphs for Matrix Multiplication', ISSAC 2023, arXiv:2212.01175, Table 1 and Arai, Ichikawa, Hukushima, ISSAC 2024 (arXiv:2312.16960).

rank_344.source: A. V. Smirnov (2013); unchanged in M. Kauers and J. Moosbauer, 'Flip Graphs for Matrix Multiplication', ISSAC 2023, arXiv:2212.01175, Table 1 and Arai, Ichikawa, Hukushima, ISSAC 2024 (arXiv:2312.16960).

rank_345.source: Fawzi et al., 'Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning' (AlphaTensor), Nature 610 (2022); unchanged in M. Kauers and J. Moosbauer, 'Flip Graphs for Matrix Multiplication', ISSAC 2023, arXiv:2212.01175, Table 1 and arXiv:2312.16960.

rank_355.source: A. Sedoglavic and A. V. Smirnov (2021), as cited in M. Kauers and J. Moosbauer, 'Flip Graphs for Matrix Multiplication', ISSAC 2023, arXiv:2212.01175, Table 1; unchanged in arXiv:2312.16960.

rank_445.source: M. Kauers and J. Moosbauer, 'Flip Graphs for Matrix Multiplication', ISSAC 2023, arXiv:2212.01175, Table 1: rank 60 for <4,4,5> over Z2 (valid only mod 2; AlphaTensor's 63 was the previous best). Arai, Ichikawa, Hukushima (arXiv:2312.16960) also reach 60.
rank_445.note: The seed (63) is AlphaTensor's 2022 value; 60 has been public since Dec 2022.

reduce_rank.source: Fawzi et al. (AlphaTensor), Nature 610 (2022): rank 47 for 4x4 over F2; still the best known over Z2 in M. Kauers and J. Moosbauer, 'Flip Graphs for Matrix Multiplication', ISSAC 2023, arXiv:2212.01175, Table 1 and Arai, Ichikawa, Hukushima (arXiv:2312.16960).

sort_n9.source: Best known 25 comparators (Floyd/Knuth); optimality proven by Codish, Cruz-Filipe, Frank, Schneider-Kamp, 'Twenty-Five Comparators is Optimal when Sorting Nine Inputs (and Twenty-Nine for Ten)', ICTAI 2014. Listed in B. Dobbelaere's SorterHunter table.

sort_n10.source: Best known 29 comparators (Floyd/Knuth); optimality proven by Codish, Cruz-Filipe, Frank, Schneider-Kamp, 'Twenty-Five Comparators is Optimal when Sorting Nine Inputs (and Twenty-Nine for Ten)', ICTAI 2014. Listed in B. Dobbelaere's SorterHunter table.

sort_n11.source: Best known 35 comparators; optimality proven by J. Harder, 'An Answer to the Bose-Nelson Sorting Problem for 11 and 12 Channels', arXiv:2012.04400 (2020). Listed in B. Dobbelaere's SorterHunter table.

sort_n12.source: Best known 39 comparators; optimality proven by J. Harder, 'An Answer to the Bose-Nelson Sorting Problem for 11 and 12 Channels', arXiv:2012.04400 (2020). Listed in B. Dobbelaere's SorterHunter table.

sort_n13.source: Best known upper bound 45 comparators, B. Dobbelaere's list of smallest and fastest sorting networks (SorterHunter, pinned upstream bertdobbelaere/SorterHunter@3d8b345). Not known to be optimal.

depth_n9.source: Optimal depth 7 for n=9: I. Parberry, 'A computer-assisted optimal depth lower bound for nine-input sorting networks', Mathematical Systems Theory 24 (1991); matching networks in Knuth TAOCP vol. 3.

depth_n11.source: Optimal depth 8 for n=11: D. Bundala and J. Závodný, 'Optimal Sorting Networks', LATA 2014, arXiv:1310.6271 (proves optimal depths for n <= 16).

depth_n13.source: Optimal depth 9 for n=13: D. Bundala and J. Závodný, 'Optimal Sorting Networks', LATA 2014, arXiv:1310.6271 (proves optimal depths for n <= 16).
